key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence stability of metal halide perovskites from accelerated ageing data, even for unseen samples.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster stability screening of perovskite materials by reducing the time needed for experimental degradation testing while retaining interpretability.
method: Collected a diverse dataset of 167 perovskite compositions and crystallinities under heat and light stress.
Featurized more than 86,000 photoluminescence spectra using a physics-informed model.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity and generalize across material groups.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on unseen samples, with the proposed method outperforming baseline benchmarks and generalizing across material groups.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and representativeness of the accelerated ageing dataset, so extrapolation to new stress regimes or chemistries should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
